english.title: Access / exit other than by official route on the Tyne and Wear Metro
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) whilst upon the Tyne and Wear Metro, where there was a notice by an entrance or exit indicating that it should be used as an entrance or exit only,

(A)_[entered or attempted to enter by that exit]_
(B)_[left or attempted to leave by that entrance]_
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 9(4) and 31(1) of the Tyne and Wear Metro Byelaws made under sections 58 and 62 of the Tyneside Metropolitan Railway Act 1973.
english.pointstoprove:
date
whilst upon the Tyne and Wear Metro
where entrance to/exit from a platform/station was via an automatic barrier
and a notice by an entrance/exit indicating that it should be used as an entrance/exit only
entered/attempted to enter by the exit OR
left/attempted to leave by the entrance

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 30 make provisions in relation to name and addresses.
(ii) Byelaw 31(2) provides powers for the removal of persons.
(iii) Byelaw 31(3) provides that when using these powers, an authorised person, including a constable, must show his/her identification if requested.
(iv) Byelaw 31(6) provides that in relation to this byelaw: An authorised person acting in the course of his duties shall not be liable for breach of this byelaw.
(vi Byelaw 31(4) provides that no person shall be subject to any penalty for breach of any of the Byelaws by disobeying a notice unless it is proved to the satisfaction of the Court before whom the complaint is laid that the notice referred to in the particular Byelaw was displayed.
(vi) Byelaw 31(5) provides that any person who attempts to breach this byelaw shall be liable to the same penalty as for the full offence.
